source_text: וַ/יַּעַן֩ אֶחָ֨ד מֵ/עֲבָדָ֜י/ו וַ/יֹּ֗אמֶר וְ/יִקְחוּ נָ֞א חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה מִן הַ/סּוּסִים֮ הַֽ/נִּשְׁאָרִים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאֲרוּ בָ/הּ֒ הִנָּ֗/ם כְּ/כָל ה/המון יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאֲרוּ בָ֔/הּ הִנָּ֕/ם כְּ/כָל הֲמ֥וֹן יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁר תָּ֑מּוּ וְ/נִשְׁלְחָ֖ה וְ/נִרְאֶֽה־־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then one of his servants answered and said[a], “Please let them take five of the horses that remain, which are left in it. Behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel who are left in it; behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel who have perished[b]. So let us send and see.”

signals.text: The verse contains a difficult and repetitive Hebrew comparison: 'they are like all the multitude of Israel who are left in it ... like all the multitude of Israel who have perished.' The translation preserves the repetition rather than smoothing it out.

source_text: וּ/לְ/אַחְאָ֛ב שִׁבְעִ֥ים בָּנִ֖ים בְּ/שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַ/יִּכְתֹּב֩ יֵה֨וּא סְפָרִ֜ים וַ/יִּשְׁלַ֣ח שֹׁמְר֗וֹן אֶל שָׂרֵ֤י יִזְרְעֶאל֙ הַ/זְּקֵנִ֔ים וְ/אֶל הָ/אֹמְנִ֥ים אַחְאָ֖ב לֵ/אמֹֽר־־׃
english_snapshot: Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria[a]. And Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the rulers of Jezreel, the elders, and the guardians of Ahab's sons, saying[b],

signals.text: Hebrew: 'to the officials of Jezreel.' Since the letters are said to be sent to Samaria, some understand this as referring to Jezreel-associated officials residing there, while some ancient versions and interpreters favor 'officials of Samaria.' The main text preserves the Masoretic wording.

source_text: וְ/אֵת֩ אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֜ה בֶּן יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ בֶּן אֲחַזְיָ֗הוּ תָּפַ֛שׂ יְהוֹאָ֥שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּ/בֵ֣ית שָׁ֑מֶשׁ ו/יבאו יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַ/יִּפְרֹץ֩ בְּ/חוֹמַ֨ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם בְּ/שַׁ֤עַר אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד שַׁ֣עַר הַ/פִּנָּ֔ה אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אַמָּֽה־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah[a], the son of Jehoash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh; then he came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

signals.text: The Hebrew consonantal text reads 'and they came to Jerusalem,' but the context and the following singular verb support the sense 'and he came to Jerusalem,' referring to Jehoash.

source_text: ה֗וּא הֵשִׁיב֙ אֶת גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ/לְּב֥וֹא חֲמָ֖ת עַד יָ֣ם הָ/עֲרָבָ֑ה כִּ/דְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֗ר בְּ/יַד עַבְדּ֞/וֹ יוֹנָ֤ה בֶן אֲמִתַּי֙ הַ/נָּבִ֔יא אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִ/גַּ֥ת הַחֵֽפֶר־־־־׃
english_snapshot: He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah[a], according to the word of Yahweh, the God of Israel, which he had spoken by the hand of his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet[b], who was from Gath-hepher.

signals.text: That is, likely the Dead Sea.

source_text: וַ/יִּקְשָׁר קֶ֜שֶׁר הוֹשֵׁ֣עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֗ה עַל פֶּ֨קַח֙ בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֔הוּ וַ/יַּכֵּ֨/הוּ֙ וַ/יְמִיתֵ֔/הוּ וַ/יִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּ֑י/ו בִּ/שְׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים לְ/יוֹתָ֖ם בֶּן עֻזִיָּֽה־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then Hoshea son of Elah conspired in a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down, put him to death, and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.

signals.text: The Hebrew reads 'in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.' This creates a chronological difficulty in the regnal data; some interpreters attempt to harmonize it with Ahaz's reign, but the translation follows the Hebrew wording.

source_text: בָּ/עֵ֣ת הַ/הִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב רְצִ֨ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֤ם אֶת אֵילַת֙ לַֽ/אֲרָ֔ם וַ/יְנַשֵּׁ֥ל אֶת הַ/יְהוּדִ֖ים מֵֽ/אֵיל֑וֹת ו/ארמים בָּ֣אוּ אֵילַ֔ת וַ/יֵּ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַ/יּ֥וֹם הַ/זֶּֽה־־־׃פ
english_snapshot: At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram[a], and drove the Judeans out of Elath[b]; and the Arameans came to Elath and have lived there to this day.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Arameans.' Some interpreters and ancient witnesses favor 'Edomites,' likely because that reading fits the broader context and the parallel account in 2 Chronicles 28:17.

source_text: וַ/יְצַ֨ו מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֜וּר לֵ/אמֹ֗ר הֹלִ֤יכוּ שָׁ֨מָּ/ה֙ אֶחָ֤ד מֵ/הַ/כֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִגְלִיתֶ֣ם מִ/שָּׁ֔ם וְ/יֵלְכ֖וּ וְ/יֵ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֑ם וְ/יֹרֵ֕/ם אֶת מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָ/אָֽרֶץ־־׃
english_snapshot: Then the king of Assyria commanded[a], saying, “Take there one of the priests whom you exiled from there, and let him go and live there[e][d][c][b], and let him teach them the custom of the god of the land.”

signals.text: Hebrew has plural verbs here ('let them go' / 'let them live'), though the sense is singular: 'one of the priests' ... 'let him teach them.'

source_text: וַ/יִּהְי֣וּ עֹשִׂ֔ים גּ֥וֹי גּ֖וֹי אֱלֹהָ֑י/ו וַ/יַּנִּ֣יחוּ בְּ/בֵ֣ית הַ/בָּמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ הַ/שֹּׁ֣מְרֹנִ֔ים גּ֥וֹי גּוֹי֙ בְּ/עָ֣רֵי/הֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם יֹשְׁבִ֖ים שָֽׁם׀׃
english_snapshot: But each nation kept making its own gods[a], and they set them in the shrines of the high places that the people of Samaria had made, each nation in the cities where they lived.

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵי/הֶ֜ם רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה הַ/עַ֨ל אֲדֹנֶ֤י/ךָ וְ/אֵלֶ֨י/ךָ֙ שְׁלָחַ֣/נִי אֲדֹנִ֔/י לְ/דַבֵּ֖ר אֶת הַ/דְּבָרִ֣ים הָ/אֵ֑לֶּה הֲ/לֹ֣א עַל הָ/אֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַ/יֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ עַל הַ֣/חֹמָ֔ה לֶ/אֱכֹ֣ל אֶת חרי/הם וְ/לִ/שְׁתּ֛וֹת אֶת שיני/הם עִמָּ/כֶֽם־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then the Rabshakeh said to them[a], “Has my master sent me to speak these words only to your master and to you? Has he not also sent me to the men sitting on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”

signals.text: Hebrew literally uses coarse siege imagery: 'eat their dung and drink their urine.' Some manuscripts/traditions preserve euphemistic wording for the second expression, often rendered 'drink the water of their feet.'

source_text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַ/מֶּ֔לֶךְ אַל יַשִּׁ֥יא לָ/כֶ֖ם חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּי לֹ֣א יוּכַ֔ל לְ/הַצִּ֥יל אֶתְ/כֶ֖ם מִ/יָּדֽ/וֹ־־׃
english_snapshot: Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you[b][a], for he will not be able to deliver you from his hand.

signals.text: Hebrew 'from his hand,' an idiom for being under someone's power. The parallel in Isaiah 36:14 reads 'from my hand.'
